content.text: The text reviews liver and biliary diseases: transient glycosuria; functional jaundice caused mainly by bile-duct catarrh or obstruction; hepatic congestion and “nutmeg liver”; perihepatitis; cirrhosis and its causes, portal hypertension, ascites, hemorrhage, diagnosis, and treatment; hepatic abscess, including causes, symptoms, routes of rupture, prognosis, and aspiration; acute yellow atrophy and phosphorus poisoning; primary and secondary liver cancer; amyloid and fatty liver; and bile-duct catarrh and gall-stone formation. Treatments historically emphasize dietary restriction, laxatives, quinine, mineral or metallic remedies, supportive care, and drainage of abscesses. The text also states that Sandra journeyed to the bathroom and that John went to the kitchen.
